title: Three-tier KPI balance and fallback matrix
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-first tracker that ties three tiers of KPIs to explicit launch thresholds, owner runbooks, and fallback actions. Intended for product-ops + SRE + release leads to use during staging, canary, and first-week scale.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Reference Tier thresholds during preflight and hourly launch standups.
- If any Tier 1 threshold trips, execute the linked fallback immediately and notify #launch-ops slack.
- Tier 2 degradations require triage within 2 hours and decision whether to throttle/roll back feature flag.
- Tier 3 is monitoring & cost telemetry; track daily and include in 24/72 hour readouts.

Top-level summary (one line):
Balance product goals (activation, retention) vs. platform SLOs (availability, latency) with explicit cost guardrails and pre-authorized fallbacks.

Tiers and KPIs (definitions + rationale):
1) Tier 1 — Launch-critical platform SLOs (must hold or immediate fallback):
   - Availability (user-facing): 99.9% region-level uptime for launch routes. Rationale: user trust + critical flows.
   - Error rate (5xx) for inference routes: <0.5% over 5m sliding window.
   - Latency P95 (generation): <800ms for default latency-sensitive config; P50 <200ms.
   - Token-generation stall events: <5/min.
   Action: immediate automatic traffic diversion or feature flag off. Owner: eng-sre oncall.

2) Tier 2 — Product adoption & UX indicators (triage within 2h):
   - Activation completion rate (first minute after flow start): >= 60% for target cohort.
   - Feature dropoff: <25% mid-flow abandonment on first day cohort.
   - Conversational fallback rate (system fallback to template): <8%.
   Action: canary size reduction, rate limiting for new cohorts, enable degraded prompt path. Owner: product-hosted-api + growth PM.

3) Tier 3 — Cost & efficiency signals (daily review, informs rollout/APIs):
   - Cost per 1k requests (hosted): baseline +10% tolerance.
   - GPU utilization on Dedicated pools: target 60–85% (outside this range -> capacity or scaling tweaks).
   - Cache hit rate (prefix/KV): >45% for long-form workloads.
   Action: recommend quantization profile, batching adjustments, or model variant routing. Owner: optimize team.

Fallback matrix (compact):
- Trigger: Availability drop below 99.9% (5m).
  Threshold: Region 99.9%.
  Immediate action: Divert traffic to secondary region; scale up dedicated pool (if available); enable conservative model variant.
  Communication: post status to #launch-ops, update incident doc (PRODOPS-742).
  Rollback criteria: sustained recovery < 30m -> keep changes; >30m -> full feature flag off.
  Owner: eng-sre + release lead.

- Trigger: Latency P95 > 1200ms (10m).
  Immediate action: throttle non-essential routes, reduce batch windows, switch to lower-latency model variant.
  Communication: notify product-ops and customer-success for any active beta customers.
  Rollback criteria: latency back within 10% of baseline for 15m.
  Owner: serving-runtime + product-hosted-api.

- Trigger: Activation rate drops > 30% relative to expected baseline (1h).
  Immediate action: roll back latest UX change to previous canary cohort, open quick investigation runbook, pause new invites.
  Communication: growth channel + release lead.
  Owner: product-ops + growth PM.

Runway scenarios (probabilistic knobs to tune):
- Slow-roll safe: ramp cohorts 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 48h; pre-approve burst capacity + 2 SRE staff during the 20->50 shift.
- Aggressive ramp: 10% -> 50% within 6h only if all Tier 1 and Tier 2 stable for 2h. Auto-throttle triggers enabled.
- Emergency pause: single global feature flag and traffic gate in infra to stop all new sessions (must be tested prelaunch).

Staffing & roles (launch window):
- Release lead: coordinates go/no-go and final thumbs.
- SRE pair (oncall + standby): owns Tier 1 alerts & region actions.
- Product-ops reporter: synthesizes hourly kpi snapshot and communications.
- Solutions eng: customer escalations for top 5 beta customers.
- Optimize lead: recommends immediate batching/quantization changes for Tier 3.

Prelaunch checklist (preflight):
- [ ] Confirm automated canary metrics pipeline (alerting + dashboards) is wired to runbook.
- [ ] Smoke test failover path (secondary region) — scheduled and documented.
- [ ] Validate feature flag kill-switch works end-to-end.
- [ ] Confirm owner rotations and pager coverage for first 72h.
- [ ] Run cost-impact simulation for expected cohorts (see cost sheet link).

Canary cadence & measurement quick recipe:
- Canary size: 2–5% of daily active users for first 6h.
- Measurement windows: 15m (Tier 1), 60m (Tier 2), 24h (Tier 3).
- Pass rule: no Tier 1 violations; Tier 2 deviations allowed up to 10% if a known behavioral shift (documented).
- If pass, move to next cohort after 6h stable.

Communication templates (short):
- Slack incident header: [LAUNCH-INCIDENT] <route> degraded — immediate action: <diversion|flag-off|throttle> — owner: <name> — see PRODOPS-742
- Customer-facing: We observed degraded performance for <feature>. We have routed traffic to a mitigated path and are monitoring closely. ETA for recovery: 30–60m.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- What is the acceptable cost-per-activation lift for paid enterprise betas? (finance stake)
- Should we allow per-customer backoff rules to remain in Dedicated vs. Hosted for first 30d?
- Do we pre-authorize auto-escalation of Dedicated capacity beyond committed pool for first-week surges?

Appendix: useful links & tickets:
- Incident runbook reference: PRODOPS-742
- Launch playbook (long form): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/POP/Launch+Playbook
- Infra PR with traffic gate: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/256

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact — if you want a spreadsheet-style ledger (hour-by-hour), I can add a sheet with formulas for burn/capacity and cohort math.
- Looking for agreement on: Tier 1 latency thresholds and whether the P95 800ms target is realistic for the large-generation path (serving-runtime input needed).

Signed: Priya (product-ops)
